rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration. This experiment tests a standard multimodal setup with PCA and ResNet50 encoders, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion. It clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modal baselines, which is critical for guiding subsequent experiments.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves 0.639 validation accuracy. This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced image encoder) while keeping other parameters the same. It clarifies whether upgrading the image encoder significantly impacts performance, balancing exploitation of the previous multimodal setup with exploration of a key design choice. This is a logical extension with high potential to improve accuracy.

The existing evidence shows config_018 (validation accuracy 0.706) is the best so far, using scvi_n200 RNA, ViT-L image, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion. This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation (config_024), which could capture more complex interactions between modalities. It clarifies whether the aggregation method is a key factor for improvement, balancing exploitation of the current best configuration with exploration of a promising variation.

The existing evidence shows config_024 (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.725). This experiment tests whether switching to concat fusion (config_015) with the same RNA/image encoders and transformer aggregation could improve performance, clarifying the impact of fusion methods. It balances exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of a key design choice (fusion type) that could yield higher accuracy.

The existing evidence shows that config_024 (scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.725). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with pca_n2000 while keeping other components identical, clarifying whether the RNA encoder choice is critical. This balances exploitation of the current top-performing setup with exploration of a key design choice, prioritizing configurations that could further improve accuracy without deviating significantly from proven components.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_024) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests replacing scvi_n200 with scgpt RNA encoder while keeping other components the same, to evaluate if a different RNA encoder could further improve performance. This clarifies the impact of RNA encoder choice on accuracy, a critical design choice with limited prior testing.

Existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_024) achieve the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests a variation with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion to compare the impact of these parameters. It clarifies whether the current best's aggregation/fusion choices are optimal, balancing exploitation of proven components with exploration of alternatives under the limited budget.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (as in config_024) yield high accuracy. This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA encoder (used in top-performing config_022) with resnet50 image encoder (from config_025), maintaining transformer aggregation and weighted fusion. This clarifies if combining scvi_n200 with resnet50 outperforms the current best (config_024) and balances exploitation of proven components with exploration of RNA/image encoder pairings.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_024) achieve high accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 while retaining transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, which could further improve performance by leveraging resnet50's potential for image features. It clarifies whether image encoder choice impacts accuracy in this setup, balancing exploitation of current top performers with exploration of alternative architectures.

The existing evidence shows config_024 (0.725) is the best so far, using scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion. This experiment tests scvi_n200 with resnet50 and avgpool aggregation, which could clarify if image encoder choice (resnet50 vs. imagenet_vit_l) impacts performance. It balances exploitation of scvi_n200 and exploration of alternative image encoders, maximizing potential for incremental improvement under the final budget constraint.
